raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran the repository pre-commit hooks on the changed files and retained their formatting.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable directory Hard Rules (python/cudnn/AGENTS.md Rules 1-9; python/cudnn/sdpa/AGENTS.md S1, S2 and the placement rule; test/AGENTS.md).
- [x] Labels: cat-feature, area:frost, area:global_attention, mod-frost, mod-cutedsl, orig-nv-eng.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL SDPA backward (the d128 f16/bf16 family of `sdpa_bwd_sm100_d128`), one FE node header, Python engine
integration, tests, docs.

## Summary

Four changes to the d128 backward family. (1) The `cta_group::2` pair body gets a DENSE twin: a dense compact-BSHD BF16 GQA/MQA
declaration is served by the pair under the default per-S rule exactly like the packed one -- the same five launches over the same workspace,
the main kernel byte-identical (the setup kernel synthesizes the packed metadata from the dense extents). (2) cc 10.7 (Rubin) is admitted in the
existing row for every body it dispatches, the compile target following the device as for cc 10.3 (no kernel is copied into another arch
directory; the sm_107a renderings hash kernel-by-kernel to the sm_100a records); the pair heuristic's per-S threshold becomes part-keyed and
is re-measured on Rubin (8192 holds); a pinned deterministic override that cannot finalize on cc 10.7 becomes a decline, so the FROST
recompute row serves deterministic d128 backward there. (3) Rubin's extra TMEM and SMEM are wired in as typed, part-keyed maps of the pair body -- `tmem_map = "dq_576"` (the independent dQ image
at columns 512-575 of the 576-column carve, two barrier rows fewer) and `smem_map = "rubin_b2"` (a two-stage dS / exchange staging ring with
`dq_read_done`, sQ1 x2, sDO1 x2 in the 327 KiB carveout) -- both measured on a Rubin class node and both kept OFF by default: the TMEM map is
neutral, the SMEM ring loses (numbers below), so the shipping maps stay the SM100 ones on every part. (4) The six d128 kernels of
`kernels/sm100` and their helper and per-route host modules are consolidated into `bprop_d128_f16.py` (13 kernels in nine sections,
each old module's header kept as its section docstring) and `prepared_d128_host.py` (one `compile_host_<route>` per route, every cache key and
exported symbol unchanged); 13 modules removed, no shims; pure code motion: 54 of 54 PTX renderings (sm_100a and sm_107a, 206 per-kernel
md5s) byte-identical before and after, every committed record reproduced. This supersedes the
earlier draft of this PR, which copied one body into `kernels/sm107` under a new engine id.

## Why

The pair body (the fastest d128 backward on Blackwell at S >= 8K) served only packed THD declarations; dense GQA fell back to the one-CTA
body. Rubin had no d128 backward row; its tcgen05 feature set is the SM100 line's, so the SM100 bodies run there unchanged. The one-CTA body
and the pair body each beat the alternatives on Rubin where a backend plan exists at all (below). One kernel module replaces five kernel
files and four helper files that had grown by accretion.

## Related issues

Supersedes the previous draft content of this PR (#2086). Related: #1943 (the pair body), #1965 (the stats ring), #1964 (cc 10.3).

## API and compatibility impact

Append-only. `cta_pair` now admits dense compact-BSHD declarations (no new field; the selector's predicate is named `layout`); new typed
op-level field `tmem_map` on the pair body (`None` = the part's default, `s_tail` on every part; `dq_576` selectable by name on cc 10.7:
the independent dQ TMEM image at columns 512-575 of the 576-column carve, two barrier rows fewer, measured neutral, kept as the base of the
staging arm) and `smem_map` = "sm100" | "rubin_b2" | the diagnostic "sm100_oversized" (cc 10.7 only, off by default). `CTA_PAIR_MIN_SEQ` is a mapping per admitted cc (8192 on cc 10.0 / 10.3 / 10.7). Capabilities
row `sdpa_bwd_sm100_d128`: `sm_hi` 106 -> 107. SUPPORT_MATRIX_TRACKER.md and docs/operations/attention/sdpa_bwd_sm100_d128.md updated in the
same commits (Rule S2). Placement (the SDPA guide's placement rule): the THD d128 lead box applies on cc 10.7 as on cc 10.0 (the cuDNN backend offers no d128 THD
backward plan on cc 10.7 with 9.24 or 9.27, so the FROST row is the only candidate there); dense d128 trails on every part (parity measured
against the backend's engine on Rubin: +1.6 % at 16K, inside noise at 8K) until a placement study measures the dense pair twin. Declined by
name, unchanged: deterministic on the grouped / packed routes, FP16 grouped, windows on the pair, `dkv_accum = fp32_reduce` on the dense
pair twin, `16w_fa4` with `dq_576` / `rubin_b2`. The header change: `override_heuristics_query()` no longer pins backend engine 17 for deterministic
backward on `sm_version > 103` (it returns the "no override" value with the reason the (256, 512] band already uses); cc 10.0 / 10.3 keep
their engine-5 pin (verified). The fp8 backward node's identical branch is listed as an open item.

## Testing

RED-then-green on the pre-change tree for every new test (the commands and failure texts are in the task's retained logs). Host (login box, DSL 4.8.1): the d128 host / contract / pair modules and test_tiers green; every rendering
pin green: the sm_100a / sm_103a / sm_107a records of the pair body, the dense record rows, the dq_576 record, the seven probe md5s, the
program-order source pin. GPU: cc 10.0 (B200 dev class, 148 SMs, functional only): the pair-body heuristic module 58 passed, the pair-body +
grouped modules 89 passed at the fold head; cc 10.7 (Rubin class, 212 SMs): the d128 L0 suites 307 passed with the 10 deterministic cells
green after the header fix (51 of 51 in test_sdpa_bwd_d128_sm100.py), the dense twin 147 passed, the backward SMOKE tier 59 passed, arm R1 35
passed; the coverage rows (rectangular dense twins, dense x dq_576, dq_576 x fp32_reduce / ldg / probes) 378 passed on cc 10.7 + 155 on cc 10.0.
The squashed PR head (first form, 63de177f; the import attested under the PR tree in every process): host (login box, DSL 4.8.1) the 17
d128 / d192 modules + the tiers 1126 passed / 282 skipped (GPU rows by capability); cc 10.0 (B200 dev class, 148 SMs) `-m L0` on the
pair-body, heuristic, sm100, grouped and accum modules 252 passed / 28 skipped; cc 10.7 (Rubin class, 212 SMs) `-m L0`: the nine
non-pair d128 modules 261 passed / 3 skipped, the pair-body GPU rows 74 passed / 2 skipped, the pair-body skew children 23 passed. The amended
head re-ran the host sweep green (1127 passed / 282 skipped: the one new row is the record-selector pin). Skips are listed with reasons; the only skips that name the part under test are the two
by-design decline rows (the bitwise twin covers the map). SMOKE tier cells added for cc100 / cc103 / cc107.

## Measured

Rubin class node, 212 SMs @ 2376 MHz lock (busy clocks sampled per cell under the power cap: 1944-2136 MHz), exclusive GPU, A/B/A 3 x 100
in both build orders with a control twin, band max(1 %, |pair|), 2026-11-03; the rows of record are the reverse build order (the
conservative one), measured at the task heads fcc0a649 (pair vs one-CTA, the placement rows), e26ced25 (dq_576), 60bf3aba / 660aef69 (rubin_b2,
the carveout probe); the PR head's renderings hash to the same committed md5 records; the full record is retained internally. Speed-ups
are `base / new - 1` on the backward step (eager, same process).

| cell (bf16, causal, b 4, hq 32, hkv 4, d 128) | baseline | kernel | speed-up (+X %) | SOL % (MMA, sampled clock) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| THD uniform S 8192 | FROST one-CTA grouped body 2.901 ms | pair body 2.689 ms | +7.9 % (forward build 2.915 / 2.647 ms, +10.1 %) | 55-58 % |
| THD uniform S 16384 | one-CTA 10.744 ms | pair 9.778 ms | +9.9 % (forward 10.768 / 9.651 ms, +11.6 %) | 65 % |
| THD uniform S 32768 | one-CTA 41.642 ms | pair 37.082 ms | +12.3 % (forward 41.617 / 36.711 ms, +13.4 %) | 70 % |
| THD uniform S 4096 | one-CTA 0.851 ms | pair 0.868 ms | not a win (orders disagree) -> the one-CTA body serves | 40-46 % |
| dense MHA b 4 h 32 S 16384 | cuDNN 9.27.0.42 engine (reference venv) 10.359 ms | FROST one-CTA accumulation 10.199 ms | +1.6 % (both orders) | 59-60 % |
| dense MHA b 4 h 32 S 8192 | cuDNN 9.27.0.42 engine 2.758 ms | FROST 2.762 ms | inside noise | 53-54 % |
| THD GQA S 8K / 16K / 32K vs the backend | no backend plan on cc 10.7 (9.24, 9.27) | FROST pair body | n/a: FROST is the only provider | |
| THD uniform S 8192 / 16384 / 32768, `tmem_map="dq_576"` vs the default | default | dq_576 | neutral (inside the 1 % band, both orders) | 58-70 % |
| THD uniform S 8192 / 16384 / 32768, `smem_map="rubin_b2"` on dq_576 vs the default | default 2.654 / 9.771 / 37.163 ms | rubin_b2 2.769 / 10.019 / 38.245 ms | -4.1 / -2.5 / -2.8 % (reverse order -5.0 / -4.1 / -3.9 %): a LOSS, kept selectable, not a default | 54-65 % |
| THD uniform S 8192 / 16384 / 32768, `smem_map="sm100_oversized"` (the shipping SMEM map launched in the 327 KiB carveout) vs the default, on both TMEM maps | default | sm100_oversized | neutral (inside the band in both orders: the carveout itself costs nothing; the `rubin_b2` loss is the ring's own) | 55-70 % |
cuDNN 9.24's runtime-compiled engines carry no cc 10.7 target (its embedded NVRTC), so the attested 9.24 serves no d128 backward plan on
Rubin at all; the dense rows above use a 9.27.0.42 reference environment.

## Restack onto develop

The PR head is a merge of develop a0f7b9f4 into this branch whose tree is the task's squashed result on that develop head (tree-identical
to the task-branch commit d0d0f419 the proofs above ran against), so the diff against develop is that one commit's; develop's #2190 change
to the pair-body test is merged. The earlier draft commit stays as the branch's first commit; its `kernels/sm107` copies, its engine row
(slot 11 / id 20611, which collided with develop) and its `barrier.py` change are gone from the tree.

## Review notes

- Rule S2 tracker in the same commits. Never a tolerance widened. No log statement deleted. The compiled extension was rebuilt for the
  header change on both architectures; the extension binaries are not part of the PR.
- The shared d128 chain helpers (formerly `bprop_d128_helpers.py`, Apache-2.0 header) now sit in the MIT-headed kernel module and
  `prepared_d128_host.py` keeps its Apache-2.0 header: both first-party, flagged here for the reviewer.
- After the proof lanes ran at the squash's first form, one amend touched only the pair-body test module (the record selector: the
  installed build's record is taken only when it carries the token, RED-first `..record_selector_falls_back_to_the_release_record..`), the
  tracker (one stale clause) and docstring prose of the kernel module (no PTX change: the rendering pins re-ran green on the host).
- black -l 160; SPDX headers; new test modules carry `L0`; the probe values (`s_tail_wait_off`, `s_read_wait_off`, `exchange_off`, ...)
  are diagnostics refused by every validate path, never a capability.

## Open items

- The fp8 backward node pins the same deterministic engine on `sm_version > 103` (unexercised; the same decline applies).
- The pair-body test module (51 L0 tests, 15 fresh-process host renders among them) is run as two processes on our Rubin lanes (the GPU rows,
  then the skew children); moving the render / record / census tests into a module of their own is a follow-up (no budget was raised).
- A placement study for the dense pair twin on cc 10.0 (grid + holdout prepared); the dense d128 lead rows on cc 10.7 need a cuDNN that
  serves the part (9.27+).
- The SMEM staging ring (`rubin_b2`): inside the stamped tile loop it is 4.4 % faster (the exchange waits collapse), yet the kernel is 10 %
  slower; the loss sits outside the loop or in the SMEM pipe. The `sm100_oversized` diagnostic map (the shipping map launched in the oversized
  carveout) measured the carveout itself as free (inside the band at 8K / 16K / 32K, both orders), so the loss is the ring's own; the stamps
  name Q1 x2 (218 clk/tile) and a second dQ staging bank (183) as the open levers.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `0dd00f607c3f` against base `a0f7b9f4e8e3`.

No confirmed correctness finding in the reviewed dense-pair integration and consolidation. Review remains incomplete: independent native SM107 validation is missing for the new memory maps and deterministic backend fallback.

Validation: SM100: heuristic and dense/THD pair coverage passed 60 tests, with 4 skipped; scoped pair coverage passed 53, with 17 skipped. This includes rectangular shapes, empty sequences, persistent reuse, workspace guards and capture/rebinding. The matching-head C++ binding built successfully. Its backward ABI suite passed 744 checks, and four native graph rebind/replay cases passed. Eight native SM100 deterministic dense MHA cases passed FP64 accuracy and bitwise dQ/dK/dV checks over three eager executions and three captured replays per case. All 57 changed paths and deletions match the integration tree for the author's existing pipeline 78946526. That pipeline is still running; no duplicate run was requested.

Limitations: SM107 CI job 526399826 stopped before tests. Local SM100 results do not validate the SM107-specific maps or backend heuristic change. No controlled performance comparison or native sanitizer validation was completed. Diagnostic wait-removal launches were not run.

Review incomplete; approval is deferred.

The same commit addresses the other code-scanning alerts in the changed code (the two unused loop variables, the unused reads and trailing pipeline-state advances, the two unused `bpe` locals, the `_host` alias, the dense route's `compile_host` rebinding, the test module's import form). The seven `multiple-definition` warnings stay: they are the DSL's staged-control-flow idiom (a result variable seeded before a dynamic `if` and overwritten in every branch), and the modules this consolidation replaced carried the same pattern. The kernels' PTX is unchanged by the commit (all 54 renderings of the consolidation proof re-rendered byte-identical, 206 per-kernel md5s).

+    dq_accum = _scratch(payload, cutlass.Int64(0), cutlass.Float32, (1, rounded, heads, 128), (rounded * heads * 128, heads * 128, 128, 1))
+    delta = _scratch(payload, delta_off, cutlass.Float32, (1, heads, rounded), (heads * rounded, rounded, 1))
+    dk_part = _scratch(payload, dk_off, q.element_type, (1, rounded_k, heads, 128), (rounded_k * heads * 128, heads * 128, 128, 1))
+    dv_part = _scratch(payload, dv_off, q.element_type, (1, rounded_k, heads, 128), (rounded_k * heads * 128, heads * 128, 128, 1))
+    meta = _scratch(payload, meta_off, cutlass.Int32, (4 * batch + 4,), (1,))
+    origins = _scratch(payload, origins_off, cutlass.Int64, (len(ORIGIN_PORTS), batch), (batch, 1))
+    maps = _scratch(payload, maps_off, cutlass.Int64, (THD_MAPS_PER_SEQUENCE * batch * 16,), (1,))
+    if cutlass.const_expr(dkv_fp32):
+        # dkv_accum = fp32_reduce: the per-KV-head fp32 accumulators [1, rounded_k, Hkv, 128] carved INSIDE the bf16 per-Q-head partial regions
+        # (4 x Hkv <= 2 x Hq bytes per kv row on every grouped ratio: validate_fp32_accum_fits); the advertised workspace is unchanged
+        dk_acc = _scratch(payload, dk_off, cutlass.Float32, (1, rounded_k, kv_heads, 128), (rounded_k * kv_heads * 128, kv_heads * 128, 128, 1))
+        dv_acc = _scratch(payload, dv_off, cutlass.Float32, (1, rounded_k, kv_heads, 128), (rounded_k * kv_heads * 128, kv_heads * 128, 128, 1))
+    else:
+        dk_acc, dv_acc = None, None
+    q_lens = cute.make_tensor(q_lens_ptr, cute.make_layout((batch + 1,), stride=(1,)))
+    kv_lens = cute.make_tensor(kv_lens_ptr, cute.make_layout((batch + 1,), stride=(1,)))
+    ro_ptrs = (ro_q_ptr, ro_k_ptr, ro_v_ptr, ro_o_ptr, ro_do_ptr, ro_dq_ptr, ro_dk_ptr, ro_dv_ptr, ro_stats_ptr)
+    ro = tuple(cute.make_tensor(ptr, cute.make_layout((batch + 1,), stride=(1,))) if cutlass.const_expr(ptr is not None) else None for ptr in ro_ptrs)
+    grouped_thd_chain_host(
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        o,
+        do,
+        stats,
+        dq,
+        dk,
+        dv,
+        dq_accum,
+        delta,
+        dk_part,
+        dv_part,
+        meta,
+        origins,
+        maps,
+        q_lens,
+        kv_lens,
+        ro,
+        origin_specs,
+        lens_form,
+        batch,
+        cutlass.Int32(max_sq),
+        cutlass.Int32(max_skv),
+        scale,
+        causal,
+        stream,
+        diag_delete_dq_reduce_add,
+        dkv_fp32,
+        dk_acc,
+        dv_acc,
+    )
+
+
+def compile_host_grouped_thd(config, origin_specs, origin_dtypes, dtype, causal, sm, *, diag_delete_dq_reduce_add=False, dkv_accum=None):
+    """Capacities and bounds are runtime scalars, never artifact key values.
+
+    ``diag_delete_dq_reduce_add`` (DIAGNOSTIC, default False) renders the shipped kernels under the unchanged cache key; the
+    armed build (dQ stays zero by design) is keyed apart so it can never be served to a default plan.  ``dkv_accum`` (the op-level
+    field: a ``DKV_ACCUM_FORMS`` name or ``None`` = ``bf16_partials``, the shipped chain under the unchanged key; typed, a ``ValueError``
+    by name) keys the ``fp32_reduce`` chain apart (every threaded Constexpr is in the key)."""
+    form = resolve_dkv_accum(dkv_accum)
+    fp32 = dkv_accum_fp32(form)
+    if fp32:
+        validate_fp32_accum_fits(config[1], config[2])
+    key = ("sdpa_bwd_sm100_d128_grouped_thd", GROUPED_ABI_VERSION, config, origin_specs, origin_dtypes, str(dtype), bool(causal), sm)
+    if diag_delete_dq_reduce_add:
+        key += ("diag_delete_dq_reduce_add",)
+    if fp32:
+        key += ("dkv_accum", form)
+    types = [dtype] * 5 + [cutlass.Float32] + [dtype] * 3 + [cutlass.Int32] * 2
+    args = [cute.runtime.make_ptr(t, 16, cute.AddressSpace.gmem, assumed_align=4 if i == 5 or i >= 9 else 16) for i, t in enumerate(types)]
+    ro_types = {"int32": (cutlass.Int32, 4), "int64": (cutlass.Int64, 8)}
+    args += [
+        None if name is None else cute.runtime.make_ptr(ro_types[name][0], 16, cute.AddressSpace.gmem, assumed_align=ro_types[name][1])
+        for name in origin_dtypes
+    ]
+    return compile_cached(
+        host_grouped_thd,
+        *([cutlass.Int64(0)] * 7),
+        *args,
+        cutlass.Int64(0),
+        cutlass.Float32(1),
+        cutlass.Int32(0),
+        config,
+        origin_specs,
+        bool(causal),
+        cute.runtime.make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=False),
+        bool(diag_delete_dq_reduce_add),
+        fp32,
+        options=f"--enable-tvm-ffi --gpu-arch sm_{sm}a",
+        cache_key=repr(key),
+        symbol="frost_sdpa_bwd_sm100_d128_grouped_thd_prepared",
+    )
+
+
+# ======================================================================================================================
+# route grouped_2cta (was kernels/sm100/prepared_d128_grouped_2cta_host.py)
+# ======================================================================================================================
+"""Pointer entry for grouped d128 on the cta_group::2 datapath (compact native partials, nine per-sequence maps): the packed THD chain and its
+dense compact-BSHD twin (``layout`` = "thd" | "dense", by NAME in the key; the dense form binds no length / offset operands and the setup
+kernel synthesizes the metadata from the declared extents -- ``d128_grouped_2cta_contract`` module docstring)."""
+
+_SMEM_MAP_NAMES = {code: name for name, code in SMEM_MAP_CODES.items()}  # the body's smem_map_code -> the resolved map name
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def host_grouped_2cta(
+    t_q: cutlass.Int64,
+    t_kv: cutlass.Int64,
+    t_q_phys: cutlass.Int64,
+    t_kv_phys: cutlass.Int64,
+    max_sq: cutlass.Int64,
+    max_skv: cutlass.Int64,
+    stats_head_stride: cutlass.Int64,
+    q_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    k_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    v_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    o_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    do_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    stats_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    dq_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    dk_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    dv_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    q_lens_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    kv_lens_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_q_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_k_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_v_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_o_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_do_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_dq_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_dk_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_dv_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_stats_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    workspace: cutlass.Int64,
+    scale: cutlass.Float32,
+    lens_form: cutlass.Int32,
+    config: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    origin_specs: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    causal: cutlass.Constexpr[bool],
+    diag_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    roles_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    mask_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    stats_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    layout_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    tmem_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    smem_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    dkv_fp32: cutlass.Constexpr[bool],
+    debug_clk: cutlass.Constexpr[bool],
+    stream: driver.CUstream,
+):
+    batch, heads, kv_heads, token_major = config
+    q, k, v = _io(q_ptr, t_q_phys, heads), _io(k_ptr, t_kv_phys, kv_heads), _io(v_ptr, t_kv_phys, kv_heads)
+    o, do = _io(o_ptr, t_q_phys, heads), _io(do_ptr, t_q_phys, heads)
+    dq, dk, dv = _io(dq_ptr, t_q_phys, heads), _io(dk_ptr, t_kv_phys, kv_heads), _io(dv_ptr, t_kv_phys, kv_heads)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(token_major):
+        stats = cute.make_tensor(stats_ptr, cute.make_layout((t_q_phys, heads), stride=(heads, 1)))
+    else:
+        stats = cute.make_tensor(stats_ptr, cute.make_layout((1, heads, stats_head_stride), stride=(heads * stats_head_stride, stats_head_stride, 1)))
+    payload = (workspace + cutlass.Int64(255)) & cutlass.Int64(-256)
+    tma_ring = stats_code == STATS_FORM_CODES["tma_ring"]  # the s_tail body's stats form (header section 11): the padded stats region replaces delta
+    # the pair body's TMEM map (header section 9) and SMEM map (section 8), PART-KEYED: the workspace depends on neither, the STAMPS record on both
+    dq576 = tmem_code == TMEM_MAP_CODES["dq_576"]
+    b2 = smem_code == SMEM_MAP_CODES["rubin_b2"]  # noqa: F841 (the map name below is the code space's)

raw_graphql_pull_request.title: frost(sdpa bwd d128): the dense twin of the cta_group::2 pair body, the d128 backward family on Rubin (cc 10.7), one kernel module

repo.description: cuDNN Frontend is NVIDIA's modern, open-source entry point to the cuDNN library and a growing collection of high-performance open-source kernels.
repo.name: cudnn-frontend

detail.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran the repository pre-commit hooks on the changed files and retained their formatting.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable directory Hard Rules (python/cudnn/AGENTS.md Rules 1-9; python/cudnn/sdpa/AGENTS.md S1, S2 and the placement rule; test/AGENTS.md).
- [x] Labels: cat-feature, area:frost, area:global_attention, mod-frost, mod-cutedsl, orig-nv-eng.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL SDPA backward (the d128 f16/bf16 family of `sdpa_bwd_sm100_d128`), one FE node header, Python engine
integration, tests, docs.

## Summary

Four changes to the d128 backward family. (1) The `cta_group::2` pair body gets a DENSE twin: a dense compact-BSHD BF16 GQA/MQA
declaration is served by the pair under the default per-S rule exactly like the packed one -- the same five launches over the same workspace,
the main kernel byte-identical (the setup kernel synthesizes the packed metadata from the dense extents). (2) cc 10.7 (Rubin) is admitted in the
existing row for every body it dispatches, the compile target following the device as for cc 10.3 (no kernel is copied into another arch
directory; the sm_107a renderings hash kernel-by-kernel to the sm_100a records); the pair heuristic's per-S threshold becomes part-keyed and
is re-measured on Rubin (8192 holds); a pinned deterministic override that cannot finalize on cc 10.7 becomes a decline, so the FROST
recompute row serves deterministic d128 backward there. (3) Rubin's extra TMEM and SMEM are wired in as typed, part-keyed maps of the pair body -- `tmem_map = "dq_576"` (the independent dQ image
at columns 512-575 of the 576-column carve, two barrier rows fewer) and `smem_map = "rubin_b2"` (a two-stage dS / exchange staging ring with
`dq_read_done`, sQ1 x2, sDO1 x2 in the 327 KiB carveout) -- both measured on a Rubin class node and both kept OFF by default: the TMEM map is
neutral, the SMEM ring loses (numbers below), so the shipping maps stay the SM100 ones on every part. (4) The six d128 kernels of
`kernels/sm100` and their helper and per-route host modules are consolidated into `bprop_d128_f16.py` (13 kernels in nine sections,
each old module's header kept as its section docstring) and `prepared_d128_host.py` (one `compile_host_<route>` per route, every cache key and
exported symbol unchanged); 13 modules removed, no shims; pure code motion: 54 of 54 PTX renderings (sm_100a and sm_107a, 206 per-kernel
md5s) byte-identical before and after, every committed record reproduced. This supersedes the
earlier draft of this PR, which copied one body into `kernels/sm107` under a new engine id.

## Why

The pair body (the fastest d128 backward on Blackwell at S >= 8K) served only packed THD declarations; dense GQA fell back to the one-CTA
body. Rubin had no d128 backward row; its tcgen05 feature set is the SM100 line's, so the SM100 bodies run there unchanged. The one-CTA body
and the pair body each beat the alternatives on Rubin where a backend plan exists at all (below). One kernel module replaces five kernel
files and four helper files that had grown by accretion.

## Related issues

Supersedes the previous draft content of this PR (#2086). Related: #1943 (the pair body), #1965 (the stats ring), #1964 (cc 10.3).

## API and compatibility impact

Append-only. `cta_pair` now admits dense compact-BSHD declarations (no new field; the selector's predicate is named `layout`); new typed
op-level field `tmem_map` on the pair body (`None` = the part's default, `s_tail` on every part; `dq_576` selectable by name on cc 10.7:
the independent dQ TMEM image at columns 512-575 of the 576-column carve, two barrier rows fewer, measured neutral, kept as the base of the
staging arm) and `smem_map` = "sm100" | "rubin_b2" | the diagnostic "sm100_oversized" (cc 10.7 only, off by default). `CTA_PAIR_MIN_SEQ` is a mapping per admitted cc (8192 on cc 10.0 / 10.3 / 10.7). Capabilities
row `sdpa_bwd_sm100_d128`: `sm_hi` 106 -> 107. SUPPORT_MATRIX_TRACKER.md and docs/operations/attention/sdpa_bwd_sm100_d128.md updated in the
same commits (Rule S2). Placement (the SDPA guide's placement rule): the THD d128 lead box applies on cc 10.7 as on cc 10.0 (the cuDNN backend offers no d128 THD
backward plan on cc 10.7 with 9.24 or 9.27, so the FROST row is the only candidate there); dense d128 trails on every part (parity measured
against the backend's engine on Rubin: +1.6 % at 16K, inside noise at 8K) until a placement study measures the dense pair twin. Declined by
name, unchanged: deterministic on the grouped / packed routes, FP16 grouped, windows on the pair, `dkv_accum = fp32_reduce` on the dense
pair twin, `16w_fa4` with `dq_576` / `rubin_b2`. The header change: `override_heuristics_query()` no longer pins backend engine 17 for deterministic
backward on `sm_version > 103` (it returns the "no override" value with the reason the (256, 512] band already uses); cc 10.0 / 10.3 keep
their engine-5 pin (verified). The fp8 backward node's identical branch is listed as an open item.

## Testing

RED-then-green on the pre-change tree for every new test (the commands and failure texts are in the task's retained logs). Host (login box, DSL 4.8.1): the d128 host / contract / pair modules and test_tiers green; every rendering
pin green: the sm_100a / sm_103a / sm_107a records of the pair body, the dense record rows, the dq_576 record, the seven probe md5s, the
program-order source pin. GPU: cc 10.0 (B200 dev class, 148 SMs, functional only): the pair-body heuristic module 58 passed, the pair-body +
grouped modules 89 passed at the fold head; cc 10.7 (Rubin class, 212 SMs): the d128 L0 suites 307 passed with the 10 deterministic cells
green after the header fix (51 of 51 in test_sdpa_bwd_d128_sm100.py), the dense twin 147 passed, the backward SMOKE tier 59 passed, arm R1 35
passed; the coverage rows (rectangular dense twins, dense x dq_576, dq_576 x fp32_reduce / ldg / probes) 378 passed on cc 10.7 + 155 on cc 10.0.
The squashed PR head (first form, 63de177f; the import attested under the PR tree in every process): host (login box, DSL 4.8.1) the 17
d128 / d192 modules + the tiers 1126 passed / 282 skipped (GPU rows by capability); cc 10.0 (B200 dev class, 148 SMs) `-m L0` on the
pair-body, heuristic, sm100, grouped and accum modules 252 passed / 28 skipped; cc 10.7 (Rubin class, 212 SMs) `-m L0`: the nine
non-pair d128 modules 261 passed / 3 skipped, the pair-body GPU rows 74 passed / 2 skipped, the pair-body skew children 23 passed. The amended
head re-ran the host sweep green (1127 passed / 282 skipped: the one new row is the record-selector pin). Skips are listed with reasons; the only skips that name the part under test are the two
by-design decline rows (the bitwise twin covers the map). SMOKE tier cells added for cc100 / cc103 / cc107.

## Measured

Rubin class node, 212 SMs @ 2376 MHz lock (busy clocks sampled per cell under the power cap: 1944-2136 MHz), exclusive GPU, A/B/A 3 x 100
in both build orders with a control twin, band max(1 %, |pair|), 2026-11-03; the rows of record are the reverse build order (the
conservative one), measured at the task heads fcc0a649 (pair vs one-CTA, the placement rows), e26ced25 (dq_576), 60bf3aba / 660aef69 (rubin_b2,
the carveout probe); the PR head's renderings hash to the same committed md5 records; the full record is retained internally. Speed-ups
are `base / new - 1` on the backward step (eager, same process).

| cell (bf16, causal, b 4, hq 32, hkv 4, d 128) | baseline | kernel | speed-up (+X %) | SOL % (MMA, sampled clock) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| THD uniform S 8192 | FROST one-CTA grouped body 2.901 ms | pair body 2.689 ms | +7.9 % (forward build 2.915 / 2.647 ms, +10.1 %) | 55-58 % |
| THD uniform S 16384 | one-CTA 10.744 ms | pair 9.778 ms | +9.9 % (forward 10.768 / 9.651 ms, +11.6 %) | 65 % |
| THD uniform S 32768 | one-CTA 41.642 ms | pair 37.082 ms | +12.3 % (forward 41.617 / 36.711 ms, +13.4 %) | 70 % |
| THD uniform S 4096 | one-CTA 0.851 ms | pair 0.868 ms | not a win (orders disagree) -> the one-CTA body serves | 40-46 % |
| dense MHA b 4 h 32 S 16384 | cuDNN 9.27.0.42 engine (reference venv) 10.359 ms | FROST one-CTA accumulation 10.199 ms | +1.6 % (both orders) | 59-60 % |
| dense MHA b 4 h 32 S 8192 | cuDNN 9.27.0.42 engine 2.758 ms | FROST 2.762 ms | inside noise | 53-54 % |
| THD GQA S 8K / 16K / 32K vs the backend | no backend plan on cc 10.7 (9.24, 9.27) | FROST pair body | n/a: FROST is the only provider | |
| THD uniform S 8192 / 16384 / 32768, `tmem_map="dq_576"` vs the default | default | dq_576 | neutral (inside the 1 % band, both orders) | 58-70 % |
| THD uniform S 8192 / 16384 / 32768, `smem_map="rubin_b2"` on dq_576 vs the default | default 2.654 / 9.771 / 37.163 ms | rubin_b2 2.769 / 10.019 / 38.245 ms | -4.1 / -2.5 / -2.8 % (reverse order -5.0 / -4.1 / -3.9 %): a LOSS, kept selectable, not a default | 54-65 % |
| THD uniform S 8192 / 16384 / 32768, `smem_map="sm100_oversized"` (the shipping SMEM map launched in the 327 KiB carveout) vs the default, on both TMEM maps | default | sm100_oversized | neutral (inside the band in both orders: the carveout itself costs nothing; the `rubin_b2` loss is the ring's own) | 55-70 % |
cuDNN 9.24's runtime-compiled engines carry no cc 10.7 target (its embedded NVRTC), so the attested 9.24 serves no d128 backward plan on
Rubin at all; the dense rows above use a 9.27.0.42 reference environment.

## Restack onto develop

The PR head is a merge of develop a0f7b9f4 into this branch whose tree is the task's squashed result on that develop head (tree-identical
to the task-branch commit d0d0f419 the proofs above ran against), so the diff against develop is that one commit's; develop's #2190 change
to the pair-body test is merged. The earlier draft commit stays as the branch's first commit; its `kernels/sm107` copies, its engine row
(slot 11 / id 20611, which collided with develop) and its `barrier.py` change are gone from the tree.

## Review notes

- Rule S2 tracker in the same commits. Never a tolerance widened. No log statement deleted. The compiled extension was rebuilt for the
  header change on both architectures; the extension binaries are not part of the PR.
- The shared d128 chain helpers (formerly `bprop_d128_helpers.py`, Apache-2.0 header) now sit in the MIT-headed kernel module and
  `prepared_d128_host.py` keeps its Apache-2.0 header: both first-party, flagged here for the reviewer.
- After the proof lanes ran at the squash's first form, one amend touched only the pair-body test module (the record selector: the
  installed build's record is taken only when it carries the token, RED-first `..record_selector_falls_back_to_the_release_record..`), the
  tracker (one stale clause) and docstring prose of the kernel module (no PTX change: the rendering pins re-ran green on the host).
- black -l 160; SPDX headers; new test modules carry `L0`; the probe values (`s_tail_wait_off`, `s_read_wait_off`, `exchange_off`, ...)
  are diagnostics refused by every validate path, never a capability.

## Open items

- The fp8 backward node pins the same deterministic engine on `sm_version > 103` (unexercised; the same decline applies).
- The pair-body test module (51 L0 tests, 15 fresh-process host renders among them) is run as two processes on our Rubin lanes (the GPU rows,
  then the skew children); moving the render / record / census tests into a module of their own is a follow-up (no budget was raised).
- A placement study for the dense pair twin on cc 10.0 (grid + holdout prepared); the dense d128 lead rows on cc 10.7 need a cuDNN that
  serves the part (9.27+).
- The SMEM staging ring (`rubin_b2`): inside the stamped tile loop it is 4.4 % faster (the exchange waits collapse), yet the kernel is 10 %
  slower; the loss sits outside the loop or in the SMEM pipe. The `sm100_oversized` diagnostic map (the shipping map launched in the oversized
  carveout) measured the carveout itself as free (inside the band at 8K / 16K / 32K, both orders), so the loss is the ring's own; the stamps

+    """A dense compact-BSHD GQA declaration (B, H, S, 128) strides (S*H*128, 128, H*128, 1) with contiguous Stats (B, H, S, 1); ``pad_batch`` declares

inline_comments.body: Fixed in 1d90b09b: the flag is gone and the comment it carried stays. The same commit addresses the other code-scanning alerts in the changed code (the two unused loop variables, the unused reads and trailing pipeline-state advances, the two unused `bpe` locals, the `_host` alias, the dense route's `compile_host` rebinding, the test module's import form). The seven `multiple-definition` warnings stay: they are the DSL's staged-control-flow idiom (a result variable seeded before a dynamic `if` and overwritten in every branch), and the modules this consolidation replaced carried the same pattern. The kernels' PTX is unchanged by the commit (all 54 renderings of the consolidation proof re-rendered byte-identical, 206 per-kernel md5s).

+    dq, dk, dv = _io(dq_ptr, t_q_phys, heads), _io(dk_ptr, t_kv_phys, kv_heads), _io(dv_ptr, t_kv_phys, kv_heads)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(token_major):
+        stats = cute.make_tensor(stats_ptr, cute.make_layout((t_q_phys, heads), stride=(heads, 1)))
+    else:
+        stats = cute.make_tensor(stats_ptr, cute.make_layout((1, heads, stats_head_stride), stride=(heads * stats_head_stride, stats_head_stride, 1)))
+    payload = (workspace + cutlass.Int64(255)) & cutlass.Int64(-256)
+    rounded, rounded_k, delta_off, meta_off, origins_off, maps_off, dk_off, dv_off, _ = grouped_thd_workspace_offsets(batch, heads, t_q, t_kv)
+    dq_accum = _scratch(payload, cutlass.Int64(0), cutlass.Float32, (1, rounded, heads, 128), (rounded * heads * 128, heads * 128, 128, 1))
+    delta = _scratch(payload, delta_off, cutlass.Float32, (1, heads, rounded), (heads * rounded, rounded, 1))
+    dk_part = _scratch(payload, dk_off, q.element_type, (1, rounded_k, heads, 128), (rounded_k * heads * 128, heads * 128, 128, 1))
+    dv_part = _scratch(payload, dv_off, q.element_type, (1, rounded_k, heads, 128), (rounded_k * heads * 128, heads * 128, 128, 1))
+    meta = _scratch(payload, meta_off, cutlass.Int32, (4 * batch + 4,), (1,))
+    origins = _scratch(payload, origins_off, cutlass.Int64, (len(ORIGIN_PORTS), batch), (batch, 1))
+    maps = _scratch(payload, maps_off, cutlass.Int64, (THD_MAPS_PER_SEQUENCE * batch * 16,), (1,))
+    if cutlass.const_expr(dkv_fp32):
+        # dkv_accum = fp32_reduce: the per-KV-head fp32 accumulators [1, rounded_k, Hkv, 128] carved INSIDE the bf16 per-Q-head partial regions
+        # (4 x Hkv <= 2 x Hq bytes per kv row on every grouped ratio: validate_fp32_accum_fits); the advertised workspace is unchanged
+        dk_acc = _scratch(payload, dk_off, cutlass.Float32, (1, rounded_k, kv_heads, 128), (rounded_k * kv_heads * 128, kv_heads * 128, 128, 1))
+        dv_acc = _scratch(payload, dv_off, cutlass.Float32, (1, rounded_k, kv_heads, 128), (rounded_k * kv_heads * 128, kv_heads * 128, 128, 1))
+    else:
+        dk_acc, dv_acc = None, None
+    q_lens = cute.make_tensor(q_lens_ptr, cute.make_layout((batch + 1,), stride=(1,)))
+    kv_lens = cute.make_tensor(kv_lens_ptr, cute.make_layout((batch + 1,), stride=(1,)))
+    ro_ptrs = (ro_q_ptr, ro_k_ptr, ro_v_ptr, ro_o_ptr, ro_do_ptr, ro_dq_ptr, ro_dk_ptr, ro_dv_ptr, ro_stats_ptr)
+    ro = tuple(cute.make_tensor(ptr, cute.make_layout((batch + 1,), stride=(1,))) if cutlass.const_expr(ptr is not None) else None for ptr in ro_ptrs)
+    grouped_thd_chain_host(
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        o,
+        do,
+        stats,
+        dq,
+        dk,
+        dv,
+        dq_accum,
+        delta,
+        dk_part,
+        dv_part,
+        meta,
+        origins,
+        maps,
+        q_lens,
+        kv_lens,
+        ro,
+        origin_specs,
+        lens_form,
+        batch,
+        cutlass.Int32(max_sq),
+        cutlass.Int32(max_skv),
+        scale,
+        causal,
+        stream,
+        diag_delete_dq_reduce_add,
+        dkv_fp32,
+        dk_acc,
+        dv_acc,
+    )
+
+
+def compile_host_grouped_thd(config, origin_specs, origin_dtypes, dtype, causal, sm, *, diag_delete_dq_reduce_add=False, dkv_accum=None):
+    """Capacities and bounds are runtime scalars, never artifact key values.
+
+    ``diag_delete_dq_reduce_add`` (DIAGNOSTIC, default False) renders the shipped kernels under the unchanged cache key; the
+    armed build (dQ stays zero by design) is keyed apart so it can never be served to a default plan.  ``dkv_accum`` (the op-level
+    field: a ``DKV_ACCUM_FORMS`` name or ``None`` = ``bf16_partials``, the shipped chain under the unchanged key; typed, a ``ValueError``
+    by name) keys the ``fp32_reduce`` chain apart (every threaded Constexpr is in the key)."""
+    form = resolve_dkv_accum(dkv_accum)
+    fp32 = dkv_accum_fp32(form)
+    if fp32:
+        validate_fp32_accum_fits(config[1], config[2])
+    key = ("sdpa_bwd_sm100_d128_grouped_thd", GROUPED_ABI_VERSION, config, origin_specs, origin_dtypes, str(dtype), bool(causal), sm)
+    if diag_delete_dq_reduce_add:
+        key += ("diag_delete_dq_reduce_add",)
+    if fp32:
+        key += ("dkv_accum", form)
+    types = [dtype] * 5 + [cutlass.Float32] + [dtype] * 3 + [cutlass.Int32] * 2
+    args = [cute.runtime.make_ptr(t, 16, cute.AddressSpace.gmem, assumed_align=4 if i == 5 or i >= 9 else 16) for i, t in enumerate(types)]
+    ro_types = {"int32": (cutlass.Int32, 4), "int64": (cutlass.Int64, 8)}
+    args += [
+        None if name is None else cute.runtime.make_ptr(ro_types[name][0], 16, cute.AddressSpace.gmem, assumed_align=ro_types[name][1])
+        for name in origin_dtypes
+    ]
+    return compile_cached(
+        host_grouped_thd,
+        *([cutlass.Int64(0)] * 7),
+        *args,
+        cutlass.Int64(0),
+        cutlass.Float32(1),
+        cutlass.Int32(0),
+        config,
+        origin_specs,
+        bool(causal),
+        cute.runtime.make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=False),
+        bool(diag_delete_dq_reduce_add),
+        fp32,
+        options=f"--enable-tvm-ffi --gpu-arch sm_{sm}a",
+        cache_key=repr(key),
+        symbol="frost_sdpa_bwd_sm100_d128_grouped_thd_prepared",
+    )
+
+
+# ======================================================================================================================
+# route grouped_2cta (was kernels/sm100/prepared_d128_grouped_2cta_host.py)
+# ======================================================================================================================
+"""Pointer entry for grouped d128 on the cta_group::2 datapath (compact native partials, nine per-sequence maps): the packed THD chain and its
+dense compact-BSHD twin (``layout`` = "thd" | "dense", by NAME in the key; the dense form binds no length / offset operands and the setup
+kernel synthesizes the metadata from the declared extents -- ``d128_grouped_2cta_contract`` module docstring)."""
+
+_SMEM_MAP_NAMES = {code: name for name, code in SMEM_MAP_CODES.items()}  # the body's smem_map_code -> the resolved map name
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def host_grouped_2cta(
+    t_q: cutlass.Int64,
+    t_kv: cutlass.Int64,
+    t_q_phys: cutlass.Int64,
+    t_kv_phys: cutlass.Int64,
+    max_sq: cutlass.Int64,
+    max_skv: cutlass.Int64,
+    stats_head_stride: cutlass.Int64,
+    q_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    k_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    v_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    o_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    do_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    stats_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    dq_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    dk_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    dv_ptr: cute.Pointer,
+    q_lens_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    kv_lens_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_q_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_k_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_v_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_o_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_do_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_dq_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_dk_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_dv_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    ro_stats_ptr: Optional[cute.Pointer],
+    workspace: cutlass.Int64,
+    scale: cutlass.Float32,
+    lens_form: cutlass.Int32,
+    config: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    origin_specs: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    causal: cutlass.Constexpr[bool],
+    diag_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    roles_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    mask_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    stats_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    layout_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    tmem_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    smem_code: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    dkv_fp32: cutlass.Constexpr[bool],
+    debug_clk: cutlass.Constexpr[bool],
+    stream: driver.CUstream,
+):
+    batch, heads, kv_heads, token_major = config
+    q, k, v = _io(q_ptr, t_q_phys, heads), _io(k_ptr, t_kv_phys, kv_heads), _io(v_ptr, t_kv_phys, kv_heads)
+    o, do = _io(o_ptr, t_q_phys, heads), _io(do_ptr, t_q_phys, heads)
+    dq, dk, dv = _io(dq_ptr, t_q_phys, heads), _io(dk_ptr, t_kv_phys, kv_heads), _io(dv_ptr, t_kv_phys, kv_heads)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(token_major):
+        stats = cute.make_tensor(stats_ptr, cute.make_layout((t_q_phys, heads), stride=(heads, 1)))
+    else:
+        stats = cute.make_tensor(stats_ptr, cute.make_layout((1, heads, stats_head_stride), stride=(heads * stats_head_stride, stats_head_stride, 1)))
+    payload = (workspace + cutlass.Int64(255)) & cutlass.Int64(-256)
+    tma_ring = stats_code == STATS_FORM_CODES["tma_ring"]  # the s_tail body's stats form (header section 11): the padded stats region replaces delta
+    # the pair body's TMEM map (header section 9) and SMEM map (section 8), PART-KEYED: the workspace depends on neither, the STAMPS record on both
+    dq576 = tmem_code == TMEM_MAP_CODES["dq_576"]
+    b2 = smem_code == SMEM_MAP_CODES["rubin_b2"]  # noqa: F841 (the map name below is the code space's)
